children: Peru's central bank unexpectedly held the nation's benchmark interest rate at 4.25% on Wednesday, despite analyst forecasts of a 25-basis-point hike to end the rate-hold cycle, as inflation remains above the target range and under pressure from the impact of weather conditions on domestic prices.

The central bank said its board decided to leave the rate unchanged even as annual inflation edged up to 4.5% in September from 4.4% in August, driven mainly by higher fuel and electricity prices. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, held at 4.5%.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected the bank to raise the reference rate to 4.50%, which would have marked its first increase in more than three years.

The bank said 12-month inflation expectations were unchanged at 3.1% in September, still slightly above the top of its target range, but both headline and core inflation should ease back toward 2% as supply shocks fade.
It warned, however, that El Niño weather risks and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East could keep price pressures elevated for longer.
